title: BAKER'S DOZEN: The Thirteenth Ingredient — Full Walkthrough, No Commentary
about: BAKER'S DOZEN: The Thirteenth Ingredient, played from power-on to the credits, including the opening, story, every level, and ending, with the game's music and sound effects. No commentary.

In 1776, Corporal Ebenezer Baker stole a root beer recipe from the Redcoats, and that is the real reason America won (nobody talks about it). This year Gwinn ate the card. As Doc Leo, hobo clown and root beer man, go down into Ebenezer's booby-trapped kitchen and find all twelve ingredients before the parade. And the thirteenth.

BAKER'S DOZEN: The Thirteenth Ingredient is a Sandbox Software game for Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition, a 1996 DOS-style release that runs in Recreational Software Designs' Game-Maker 3.0 (PLAYGAME) and in the web app. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) wrote and built it: the code, its pictures, music, sounds, and words. Much of it is drawn from Lewis "Lewie" Moten III: his blog writing, photos he provided, and conversations about his interests, experiences, and hobbies. Lewis directed the game and playtested it as it came together.
This video was recorded by the web app itself, frame by frame, at the game's 320×200 resolution.
